newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha up, trade quiet after aggressive sale.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha up, trade quiet after aggressive sale.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices firmed on Friday in line with overnight crude gains, but most traders kept to the sidelines after a Japanese trading house sold aggressively in late Thursday dealing, traders said.
The Japanese trader on Thursday sold first-half August to a western trader at $213.00 per tonne, which was was $1.00 to $2.00 below market levels, they said.
"Market participants are unsure where the market is heading after the aggressive selling," one naphtha trader said.
Offers for first-half August open-spec naphtha were heard at $214.50 to $215.00 against notional bids at about $213.00.

The low-priced sales prompted first-half August/first-half September to move into contango. The spread was assessed at minus 50 cents on Friday. On Thursday, spreads from first-half August onwards were discussed in backwardation.
In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR), a Japanese trader sold a June cargo at 50 to 60 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula amid expectations of tight supplies ahead.
LSWR premiums were quoted at as low as 25 cents a month ago due to ample availability caused by an accidental closure of a hydrocracker at Indonesia's Dumai refinery.
